(Today through Sunday)...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

Today Through Tuesday.

Areas of fog have developed across much of central Indiana and will 
continue to spread in coverage through daybreak with clear skies and 
calm winds across the forecast area. Fog generally remains non-dense 
but with the increasing coverage, have elected to issue a Special 
Weather Statement. Will continue to monitor observational trends 
going forward and will issue a Dense Fog Advisory if conditions 
warrant.

Strong low-level WAA will overspread the area after daybreak as 
surface high pressure shifts off the Mid-Atlantic coast and a 
deepening upper trough moves across the Northern Plains. The 
tightening regional pressure gradient will drive gusty southwesterly 
surface winds of 15 to 25 kt across the forecast area. Model 
soundings show strong boundary layer mixing up to 850 MB, where 
temperatures reaching 15-17°C will support afternoon surface highs 
in the mid to upper 80s. These values will threaten established 
record highs at IND (86F) and approach the 90F mark in the Wabash
Valley. Deep subsidence and dry mid-level air will maintain 
sub-0.8 inch PWATs, suppressing cloud cover and keeping conditions
clear through Monday night.

On Tuesday, the thermal ridge axis will remain centered over the 
Ohio Valley ahead of a cold front pushing southward out of the Upper 
Great Lakes. Deep boundary layer mixing and ongoing southwesterly 
flow will maintain unseasonable warmth with daytime highs again 
reaching the upper 80s under mostly sunny skies with another shot at 
breaking the record at IND. HREF and HRRR component members show 
moisture transport increasing late Tuesday night along a pre-frontal 
40 kt LLJ, raising PWAT values above 1.3 inches across northwestern 
counties. Low-level convergence along the sagging surface boundary 
will initiate scattered shower and elevated thunderstorm activity 
after 06Z Wednesday, while areas further southeast remain dry 
through the morning hours.

Wednesday Through Saturday.

The surface cold front will decelerate and align parallel to mid-
level southwesterly flow across central Indiana Wednesday and 
Thursday. Ensemble guidance is hinting in a prolonged precipitation 
event as multiple embedded shortwave impulses traverse the stalled 
boundary. Strong low-level baroclinic forcing combined with moisture 
advection drawing Gulf moisture northward will push PWATs above 1.5 
inches along the frontal zone, exceeding the 90th percentile for mid-
October. Diagnostic soundings indicate elevated MUCAPE between 300-
800 J/kg and 0-6 km bulk shear around 40-50 kt, supporting embedded 
thunderstorms and efficient rainfall rates along with a lower-end 
threat for severe weather. Cloud cover, precipitation, and post-
frontal CAA north of the boundary will cap Wednesday and Thursday 
highs in the upper 60s to mid 70s.

A robust upper-level trough will dig into the Eastern CONUS by 
Thursday night, driving the frontal boundary south into the 
Tennessee Valley and opening the path for strong CAA. High pressure 
of Canadian origin will build across the Northern Plains into the 
Great Lakes. Northwesterly winds will gust as high as 40 mph in the 
aftermath of the frontal passage as strong pressure gradients remain 
in place. These stronger winds will relax through the weekend as the 
high centers over the Ohio Valley. Daytime temperatures will drop to 
seasonable levels in the mid to upper 60s on Friday, cooling further 
into the upper 50s and lower 60s on Saturday and Sunday. Clear 
skies, light winds, and efficient radiational cooling over the 
weekend will allow overnight lows to fall low to mid 30s with a 
freeze possible across eastern Indiana and frost likely across all 
of central Indiana.
